about: Lab PR 236 (multi-match): a new ~/.ssh/authorized_keys created under /home by a user's program. NN-L-FIM-002 (a file created in a watched user-writable directory: Medium, recorded) used to win first-match and NN-L-FIM-004 (High, kill) was never recorded. Now both match and FIM-004 is primary (High); its kill is held by the legacy ceiling (the first-match engine ran only FIM-002's record: an administrator's ssh-copy-id is not killed) until a signed policy says `enforce NN-L-FIM-004` (policy-fim004-enforced).

switches.held: the kill of the shell's process tree (R020, lab PR 224)
the kill of one process past the scan kill threshold (NN-L-NET-026, lab PR 224)
the kill of one process past the brute-force kill threshold (NN-L-NET-027, lab PR 224)
the kill for a flow to port 53 of a server that is no configured resolver (port 53 was exempt before lab PR 224)
the kill of an allowlisted transfer tool whose lineage holds a precursor (exempt before lab PR 224)
the kill of the ransomware actor's process tree (NN-L-IMP-001, lab PR 225)
the kill of the staged program that asked a security tool off (NN-L-EVA, lab PR 225)
the kill for a rename seen only as a watched directory's new entry (NN-L-FIM-010, a match added by lab PR 225)

decision.name: SSH authorized_keys modified
decision.reasoning: SSH authorized_keys modified — backdoor persistence indicator [legacy ceiling: KillProcess held — the first-match engine ran only a record (NN-L-FIM-002_NewSuidBinary) on this event; `enforce NN-L-FIM-004` in the signed per-rule policy lifts it] [also matched: NN-L-FIM-002_NewSuidBinary (Log, Medium)]
